products.name: Cue
products.line: Read your script while looking at the lens. Cue floats the words over the camera so you never lose eye contact.
facts: Record a take, stop, and the script waits where you left it. Combine every take into one video.
Solo. Design, code, App Store, marketing site.

products.name: ClipBridge Sync
products.sub: iPhone, Android, Windows, Mac · App Store
products.line: One clipboard for every device. Copy on your phone, paste on your PC, and back. End-to-end encrypted, so the relay never sees your text.
facts: Swift and SwiftUI (iPhone), Kotlin (Android), Electron (Windows, Mac), Node.js relay over WebSockets, APNs
One encryption scheme that four platforms agree on, with a relay that only ever forwards ciphertext.
Solo. Four clients, the relay, the App Store and store listings.

products.name: NUQTA
products.sub: iPhone and Apple Watch · App Store
products.line: A casual score tally for the games you play with friends. Tap to score on your phone or your wrist, share the live board, and keep the history.
facts: Phone and watch stay in sync in both directions, even when one of them is asleep.
Solo. Phone app, watch app, widgets, App Store.

products.name: Poof
products.sub: iPhone · App Store · Made in Dubai
products.line: Poof finds copies, blurry shots, screenshots and large videos on your iPhone and clears them in a minute a day. Runs on your phone. Nothing is uploaded.
facts: Swift, SwiftUI, PhotoKit, Vision, ActivityKit, WidgetKit, StoreKit
Scanning tens of thousands of photos on device, resumable after iOS suspends the app, with honest progress in the Dynamic Island.
Solo. Engine, app, Live Activity, widgets, App Store.
Data Not Collected. No analytics, no backend.

sdk.headline: One typed, bilingual data layer for Dubai's open government data
sdk.line: Dubai publishes property, school, health and transit data in four separate silos, each with its own spelling of the same place. opendxb joins them once, in the open: an SDK, a CLI and an MCP server so an AI assistant can answer "what does it cost to live near an Outstanding school?" in one call.
facts: A community crosswalk that folds Arabic diacritics, ordinals and transliteration variants, and refuses to guess when two areas are too close.
TypeScript, Node 20, Zod, MCP SDK, Vitest (105 tests), nightly GitHub Action
Per-community aggregates committed nightly, so the repo doubles as a public record

game.title: Landing in Dubai
game.headline: An unofficial guide for people arriving in Dubai
game.line: The errands are not independent. No bank account without an Emirates ID, no DEWA without Ejari, no tenancy without a visa. People lose weeks discovering that one queue at a time. The game shows what blocks what.

ways.d: Arrival, the fork, your first 90 days as a dependency-aware path.
A walkable pixel city. Each building answers one thing you need to sort out.
Keyboard-navigable HTML. Nobody has to play a game to read a government fact.

facts: Every answer cites an official source and the date it was checked. A test fails the build if one does not. No fees, timelines or document lists, because they change.
TypeScript, Phaser 3, Vite, Vitest (44 tests). Progress in localStorage only, no accounts.

enterprise.line: Since November 2021 I have owned the Salesforce platform at a proptech company: real estate and mortgage teams across the UAE, Spain, Italy, Turkey and France. I lead the developers and I still write the code. Six pieces of that work, drawn as case studies.

cases.name: Agency Tracker
cases.tag: Partner lifecycle platform for real-estate agencies
cases.problem: Business development managers looked after hundreds of partner agencies with only aggregate numbers. Nobody could see which agency was going quiet, churning or producing without opening records one at a time.
cases.built: A mini-CRM inside Salesforce: a KPI strip, overview and at-risk tabs, a churn board bucketed by months of silence, a slide-out agency panel, and a bulk console that assigns churned agencies to a manager with a six-month activation window. Underneath, a health-score engine, role-scoped data access for BDM, manager and GM, a sharing batch, and an access-audit panel over the visit log.
cases.impact: Over 1,100 churned agencies became a worked list instead of a blind spot. Target set in the spec: know who to call in under 30 seconds. Rolled out with a partner portal and an onboarding form.

cases.name: Office TV dashboards
cases.tag: Live wallboards for the mortgage business unit
cases.problem: Managers and the office floor had no live month-to-date view of disbursed volume against target, and the learning team could not see how new joiners performed after onboarding.
cases.built: A 1080p auto-refreshing wallboard family: target versus achievement with a pace marker and run rate, per-region team bars, a top-five leaderboard, and sister boards for bank operations, credit and mortgage advisers. One thin controller reuses the existing dashboard calculations so the TV never shows a different number from the report. Plus an L&D app for 30, 60 and 90-day new-joiner cohorts, a campaign monitor, and metadata-driven configuration so managers set targets without a developer.
cases.impact: Three regions and four teams on one screen, refreshed every five minutes, with the month-to-date figure cross-checked against an independent query before launch.

cases.name: MC360: the consultant's cockpit
cases.tag: One working surface for mortgage consultants
cases.problem: Mortgage consultants found standard Salesforce navigation slow. Their leads, tasks and SLA countdowns lived on separate record pages with no single place to work from.
cases.built: A shell with segmented tabs and a persisted theme over three surfaces: a dashboard with count-up KPI cards, a source chart and an activity feed; a four-column leads board with drag-to-convert and a sortable infinite-scroll list; and a to-do focus panel with a large countdown and colour-coded urgency rails. The controller merges open tasks with active SLA records and surfaces the escalation stage, from original owner to team lead.
cases.impact: Replaced about 1,100 lines of ad-hoc page JavaScript with a token-based component system. In QA at time of writing.

cases.name: Primary Hub: a CRM suite for the sales team
cases.tag: Kanban, chat, calendar, clock-in and dashboards
cases.problem: The primary real-estate team worked leads, listings, calendars, attendance and internal messages across disconnected pages, with no shared board, no in-org chat, and no way to see who was viewing which record.
cases.built: A component suite: a metadata-driven Kanban with stage validation rules, a real-time chat stack on platform events with presence, a team calendar, clock-in and clock-out, advanced search, a properties list, commission and satisfaction dashboards, and lead conversion with team split. Page-view telemetry flows through a platform event into a visit log with a scheduled cleanup. Deployable to Experience Cloud as a partner hub.
cases.impact: One suite, six flows and four platform events, replacing a set of disconnected pages for the whole primary team.

cases.name: AI lead qualification pipeline
cases.tag: Event-driven backend with two retry tiers
cases.problem: Leads landing in the pool had to be qualified by people calling them one by one, with no guard against calling the same number twice and no view of what was in flight.
cases.built: A trigger that fires only on the transition into the pool, a handler with row locks and duplicate-phone detection, queueable and scheduled services that keep calls inside Dubai calling hours and roll to the next business day, and a callout service to the qualification API through a named credential. Two retry tiers on top: technical retries from custom settings, and business retries written to their own object. A dashboard refreshes every 30 seconds from monitor events.
cases.impact: Internal figures: manual first-call qualification cut by about 95%, and roughly 40% more leads reached thanks to the retry tiers.

cases.name: Record-access audit and reports
cases.tag: Who saw what, when, and whether they should have
cases.problem: A record-visit log existed but nobody analysed it, so nobody could say whether people were opening loan applications they had no ownership claim to.
cases.built: A Python pipeline over SOQL exports that joins the visit log to each application's six ownership fields, classifies every view as inside or outside an ownership claim, and aggregates by user, team, bank and status. Generators render executive PDF reports and per-user spreadsheets. The same schema work later became the access-audit dashboard inside Agency Tracker.
cases.impact: Over 140,000 record views analysed across six months, with the share outside any ownership claim broken down per team. Delivered to leadership as six reports; figures and names stay internal.
